claude.take: This is a read, not a recommendation. NSE is the highest-quality asset to come to an Indian IPO in years on almost every operating measure — 92.99% cash-market share, 99.79% equity futures, zero debt, ~51% PAT margin, ₹7,949 Cr of operating cash flow, ₹34,600 Cr of treasury, ₹8,662 Cr of dividends paid in FY26. It is also the only way to own Indian exchange infrastructure at scale, and the anchor book — 189 investors, LIC largest and choosing to buy rather than sell — says serious institutions are comfortable at ₹1,785. The relative-value case is real: BSE trades at ~54x for a much smaller business while NSE is being offered at ~43x. That is the entire bull thesis and it is not a weak one. The other side is equally concrete. FY26 was a down year on both revenue and profit, and the ~43x is being paid on that declining base. Options are 60.22% of operating revenue and NSE's share of that segment has gone 96.9% → 74.71% → 68.5% in roughly two years, on the revenue-densest part of the business; the multiple only works if that curve flattens, which it has not yet. 78.65% of operating revenue sits on transaction charges that a single SEBI circular can reprice, and SEBI has done exactly that once already. The co-location and dark-fibre matters are proposed-settled at ₹1,491 Cr but not closed. Nothing of the ₹22,562 Cr reaches the company. And the market's own pricing signals are softening, not firming: GMP down from ₹285 to ₹160, the band set ~10% below the ₹1,990 unlisted quote and ~26% below the ₹2,400 unlisted peak, Day-1 morning book at 0.13x. Both statements are true at once — a great business, priced for a recovery that has not yet shown up in the numbers. Which of those two facts matters more depends entirely on holding period, and that is a judgement each investor has to make for themselves.

demand.read: Two readings sit on top of each other. The anchor book is about as good as an Indian anchor book gets — 189 investors, LIC as the largest, every major domestic fund house plus GIC, ADIA, Norges and Fidelity — and at ₹6,746 Cr it is itself larger than most Indian IPOs. That is not alarming for a ₹22,562 Cr issue on a three-day book where QIB and NII money typically arrives on the last day, and the absolute rupee demand at 0.13x is already larger than most whole IPOs. Still, retail running behind NII at this stage, on the most famous name in Indian capital markets, is worth noting: the ticket is only ₹14,280, so lack of affordability is not the explanation. GMP has faded from ₹285 on 7 Sep to ₹160 today, and the ₹1,785 band prices roughly 10% below the recent ₹1,990 unlisted-market quote and ~26% below the June 2025 unlisted peak of ₹2,400 — which means unlisted holders who bought near the top are underwater at the IPO price, a known source of supply on listing.

Mahanadi Coalfields.business: Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (Sambalpur, Odisha; carved out of SECL on 3 Apr 1992; Miniratna Cat-I since 2019) is Coal India's largest and most profitable subsidiary. It mines non-coking thermal coal from the Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields via 17 mines (14 opencast, 3 underground) as of 30 Jun 2026, using ~70 surface miners with coal handling plants, silos, rapid loading systems and one washery.
